n: From the camp at Shittim, Joshua secretly sends two scouts to Jericho, the fortified city guarding the way into Canaan. They lodge with a woman named Rahab, whose house was a natural place for strangers to stay unnoticed.

f.g: “Acacias” — Israel’s camp on the plains of Moab east of the Jordan.
Some ancient interpreters suggested “innkeeper,” but the Hebrew zonah normally means prostitute.

n: Word reaches Jericho’s king that Israelite spies have arrived that night.

f.g: A local city-state ruler; Canaan had many such kings.

n: The king demands that Rahab hand them over.

f.g: Spy out the land.

n: Rahab hides the men and admits visitors came, but claims she didn’t know where they were from.

f.w: I wist not whence they were
f.g: Wist = knew. “I didn’t know where they came from.”

n: She says they left at dusk before the city gate closed and urges the soldiers to chase them. Her deception protected God’s messengers; scripture praises her faith, not the lie itself.

f.g: Wot = know.
City gates were closed at nightfall for security.

n: In truth, she had hidden them on her flat roof under flax stalks drying in the sun.

f.g: Flax was harvested in spring and dried on rooftops to make linen — fitting the Passover season of Joshua 5.

n: The searchers head toward the Jordan crossings, and the city gate is shut behind them — trapping the spies inside but also keeping pursuers out.

f.g: Shallow crossing places in the river.

n: Before the men settle for the night, Rahab goes up to speak with them.

f.g: Flat roofs served as private living space.

n: Rahab’s confession of faith: “I know the Lord has given you the land.” A Canaanite woman shows more faith than Israel’s spies did forty years earlier.

f.w: I know that the LORD hath given you the land

f.g: Melt with fear.

n: News of the Red Sea crossing and the defeat of Sihon and Og had reached Jericho forty years later.

f.w: the LORD dried up the water of the Red sea

n: Rahab’s testimony reaches its peak: Israel’s God is the God of heaven and earth. She acknowledges him as the true God.

f.w: he is God in heaven above, and in earth beneath

n: She asks the spies to swear by the Lord to show her family the same loyal kindness she showed them, with a sure sign.

f.g: Hebrew ḥesed — loyal, covenant love.
A reliable sign or pledge.

n: Her request is for her whole family: parents, siblings, and all they have.
The spies pledge their own lives for hers, on condition she keeps their mission secret. They promise to treat her with loyalty and faithfulness.

f.g: “May we die if you don’t live.”
Show ḥesed and faithfulness.

n: Her house was built into the city wall, so she lowered them out a window by a rope. Archaeologists note houses were sometimes built into casemate walls.

f.g: Her house formed part of the city’s fortification.

n: She advises them to hide in the hills west of Jericho for three days, while the pursuers search toward the river.

f.g: The rugged hills west of Jericho, full of caves.

n: The spies set terms so they won’t be guilty of breaking the oath.

f.g: We will be free from guilt.

n: The sign: tie the scarlet cord in the window, and gather all your family inside. Many Christians see the red cord as a symbol of Christ’s saving blood, like the Passover blood on the doorposts.
Those who stay inside the house will be safe; anyone who leaves is responsible for their own fate. Safety is found within the covenant boundary.

f.w: his blood shall be upon his head
f.g: He is responsible for his own death.

n: If she reveals their mission, the oath is void.

f.g: Released from the oath.

n: Rahab agrees and immediately ties the scarlet cord in the window — acting on her faith right away.

f.w: According unto your words, so be it

n: The spies hide three days in the hills while the searchers fail to find them.

f.g: Abode = stayed.

n: They return across the Jordan and report everything to Joshua.

f.g: Crossed the river.

n: Their report is full of faith, unlike the fearful report of the twelve spies years before: the Lord has given us the land; its people are terrified.

f.w: Truly the LORD hath delivered into our hands all the land
